what: released PDE-Transformer sc-s fine-tuned with the paper's recipe (upstream main.py, separate channels, one-step supervised MSE) on the task's active-matter training pool; best-validation checkpoint exported by environment/reference/pde_transformer_finetune/export_package.py and replayed through tests/main_verifier.py
protocol: task protocol: canonical split (environment/data/split.json), all 1,185 held-out cases, sealed contract; the model conditions on one frame (upstream sc-s recipe, timesteps=2), so it is given the last of the four context frames; per-dataset model, only the well/active_matter group is a real forecast

training.stopped_by: the run's six-hour wall-clock cap (timeout sent SIGTERM at epoch 7); the best-validation checkpoint (epoch 6) is the one packaged
training.initialization: released sc-s checkpoint (thuerey-group/pde-transformer @ d5889aab), i.e. an external-target reference, not a from-scratch row
deviations_from_the_recipe: batch 2 with accumulate_grad_batches 8 instead of batch 8 with 2: 11 channels at 256^2 do not fit a 40 GB card at the recipe's batch. The effective batch (16) is unchanged.
the EMA callback (decay 0.999) was removed: upstream's implementation raises "Tensor list must have at least one tensor" at the first optimizer step once the batch is reduced.

normalization.what: the fine-tune's data pipeline normalizes with MeanStdNorm (normalize_data: mean-std, normalize_const: mean-std), so the package applies the same statistics, taken from the converted training file, and inverts them on the output

metadata_class_correction.what: upstream encodes the Fields and Constants entries of physical_metadata as indices into two fixed vocabularies (pdetransformer/data/metadata_remapping.py), not positionally. A first export numbered them 1..N, which loads the right weights and runs without error while conditioning the model on embeddings the fine-tune never saw.
metadata_class_correction.note: the number reported above is the corrected one; export_package.py now calls upstream's converters

interpretation: 1.6693 on its own dataset beats the from-scratch CNextU-net (1.8857, also cut short at its cap) but stays behind persistence (1.52) and behind the released mc-s zero-shot row (1.32). Two effects hold it back: the sc-s recipe conditions on a single frame (timesteps=2) and is trained on a one-step objective, so a 30-step free-running rollout compounds error quickly, while The Well's recipe consumes four frames; and only 7 of the 50 requested epochs fit in the six-hour cap. The row is reported as a protocol-handicapped external reference, not as a ceiling.

derivation.what: recomputed on 2026-09-22 from this report's own per-dataset means after removing the corpus family 'ape2d/hyp' (upstream ships hyp.hdf5 as a content copy of diff.hdf5); per-dataset numbers are the measured ones, group means and the reward follow score.py's aggregation exactly; case counts are the canonical split's (environment/data/split.json); the per-dataset means come from the run's verifier report.json and are now embedded
